headline: Union Environment Minister presides over Workshop on Mangrove Conservation in Bhuj; Releases Key Mangrove Publications and Reviews MISHTI Progress
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Environment Minister presides over Workshop on Mangrove Conservation in Bhuj; Releases Key Mangrove Publications and Reviews MISHTI Progress

Shri Bhupender Yadav stresses Scientific, Site-Specific and Community-Led Mangrove Restoration; Launches Mangrove GIS (MGIS) Portal for Decision Support

13 SEP 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today addressed the Workshop on Mangrove Conservation, Restoration and Sustainable Management held at Bhuj, Kachchh (Gujarat). Addressing the workshop, the Minister emphasised that mangroves must be conserved as living ecosystems, given their importance for coastal biodiversity, fisheries, shoreline protection, climate resilience and livelihoods.

The workshop was also attended by and addressed by Shri Arjun Modhwadia, Cabinet Minister for Forest and Environment, Climate Change and Science & Technology, Government of Gujarat, and Shri Trikambhai Chhanga, Minister of State for Higher and Technical Education, Government of Gujarat, who reaffirmed the State Government's commitment to mangrove conservation and coastal ecosystem restoration under MISHTI.

Reviewing Gujarat's mangrove conservation efforts under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) programme, the Shri Yadav noted the emphasis on restoration, scientific management, community participation and technology-enabled monitoring. He informed that under MISHTI, Gujarat has made significant progress in mangrove restoration, with 27,652 hectares covered against the 2023–27 target of 29,250 hectares, including 12,450 hectares in the ecologically challenging Kori Creek region. He added that site-specific restoration techniques suited to the conditions of Kachchh have been adopted, alongside measures for biodiversity enhancement, seaweed cultivation and sustainable livelihoods.

On the occasion, the Minister released the Coffee Table Book on Kachchh Mangroves and the Mangroves Atlas of Gujarat, and launched the Mangrove GIS (MGIS) Portal, stating that these would strengthen science-based decision-making and monitoring of mangrove habitats across the state. Shri Yadav also felicitated the Guneri Inland Mangrove Village Biodiversity Management Committee, commending its sustained community-led conservation of the Guneri inland mangroves – a rare ecosystem thriving away from the coast – which, he noted, was declared Gujarat's first Biodiversity Heritage Site in January 2025.

The workshop was attended by senior officials of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Gujarat Forest Department, along with scientists, conservationists and representatives of local communities engaged in mangrove restoration and coastal livelihood initiatives in Kachchh.

Union Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav presided over a workshop on mangrove conservation, restoration and sustainable management in Bhuj, Kachchh, Gujarat. The event included the release of key mangrove publications, the launch of the Mangrove GIS (MGIS) Portal, and a review of Gujarat’s progress under the MISHTI programme.

- The workshop was held in Bhuj, Kachchh (Gujarat) and focused on mangrove conservation, restoration and sustainable management.
- Shri Bhupender Yadav, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, emphasized scientific, site-specific and community-led mangrove restoration.

fullText:

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addresses 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai as the Chief Guest

India will emerge as the global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years

The award recipients include exporters, manufacturers, bankers and women entrepreneurs; together, they have set new benchmarks for India’s growth

We must prepare ourselves in such a way that the entire ecosystem and the complete manufacturing value chain for lab-grown diamonds are in the hands of Indians

India should emerge as a pioneering industry in the new era of lab-grown diamonds, and the Modi Government is ready to provide all possible support to achieve this

Nine out of every ten diamonds cut and polished across the world are processed in Surat, city’s traders have not merely cut and polished diamonds; by generating employment for millions, they have also made a significant contribution to the economy and India’s exports

Mumbai, economic capital of the country, has made a significant contribution to establishing the gems and jewellery trade as a key pillar of India’s exports

The resolve of Prime Minister Modi to make India the world’s foremost nation in every sphere by 15 August 2047 has also been embraced by the 1.4 billion people of the country

Whenever India has faced a crisis, jewellery traders have always stood wholeheartedly with society and the nation

The foundation laid for these awards in 1975 has, over the past 50 years, evolved into a prestigious platform for India’s gems and jewellery industry, I congratulate everyone associated with the industry for its continuity, excellence and contribution to providing employment to millions of people

13 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai as the Chief Guest. Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi, and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the awards ceremony, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that it is a matter of great happiness for him that the Gems and Jewellery Awards, which have continuously contributed to enhancing India’s economy, prosperity and global brilliance, are being conferred on so many distinguished achievers today. He said that this initiative of the India Diamond Board is a reflection of India’s confidence, skill, prosperity and global aspirations. India will emerge as the global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that when the foundation of these awards was laid in 1975, hardly anyone could have imagined that this small initiative would, five decades later, evolve into a prestigious platform for the country’s gems and jewellery industry, and that the industry would play such a significant role in the growth of the national economy and the expansion of the MSME sector. Shri Shah said that those honoured today include exporters, manufacturers, bankers and women entrepreneurs. Together, they have set new benchmarks for India’s growth.

Shri Amit Shah said that gems and jewellery have always been an integral part of India’s identity. For over 6,000 years, gems and jewellery from India have been traded across the world. The Roman writer Pliny had written that Rome’s treasury was being depleted by its trade in Indian gems and spices, as the wealth earned by Rome was flowing to India through this trade. Shri Shah said that over the centuries, Indian artisans and craftsmen have continually added new dimensions to this tradition. During the medieval period, jewellery craftsmanship received royal patronage and reached new heights. The princely states of Rajasthan and Kolkata gave rise to the distinctive traditions of Kundan and Meenakari. Even today, Jaipur is renowned across the world as the capital of coloured gemstones. He said that any discussion on India’s gems and jewellery industry would remain incomplete without mentioning Surat. Shri Shah said that it is a fact that Surat has played a tremendous role in transforming the face of an entire industry. Nearly nine out of every ten diamonds cut and polished in the world are processed in Surat. He said that the people of Surat have not merely cut and polished diamonds; they have also demonstrated the highest standards of hard work and perseverance. The diamond merchants of Surat have not only provided employment to millions of people, enabled them to become self-reliant and made a significant contribution to the country’s economy and exports, but have also accomplished something even greater. He said that there was a time when it was believed that Kutch and Saurashtra would turn into a desert within fifty years. However, through their determination and relentless efforts to secure water for Kutch and Saurashtra, the diamond merchants of Surat also played a crucial role in saving the entire Saurashtra region.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Mumbai, the country’s financial capital, has made a significant contribution to establishing the gems and jewellery industry as a key pillar of India’s exports. The Bharat Diamond Bourse (BDB) has today emerged as a symbol of India’s gems and jewellery trade across the world.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, said that the Government led by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has brought about several transformational changes in the country over the past 12 years. He said that in 2014, India was counted among the ‘Fragile Five’; today, it is among the top five economies of the world. He said that the GDP figures for the first quarter of the current financial year were released recently, and with a growth rate of 7.8 per cent, India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world. He said that this transformation has not been limited to economic activity alone; Prime Minister Modi has worked to bring about change across every sector. He said, “Who could have imagined that a terrorist attack would be answered by entering Pakistan’s territory, and that the country would have a Prime Minister capable of taking such a decisive stand?” Whether it was the surgical strike, the air strike or Operation Sindoor, Modi Ji has pursued a defence policy that makes the enemy think twice and tremble at the very thought of attacking India. He said that whether it is the construction of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, the rejuvenation of Kedarnath or Mahakal Lok, India has accomplished what, for decades, people did not even have the courage to speak about.

Shri Amit Shah said that the transformational changes brought about by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in the field of infrastructure have given a major boost to the economy. Driven by PLI schemes and facilities aimed at promoting exports, India’s exports are continuing to surpass their own records. He said that Prime Minister Modi has given the 140 crore people of the country the confidence and resolve that by 15 August 2047, India will emerge as number one nation in the world across every sector. The people of India have also embraced this resolve. Shri Shah said that wherever global circumstances have changed and trade and commerce have required support, necessary initiatives have been undertaken. The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026 is the latest example of this. Companies engaged in the trading of rough diamonds in specially notified areas have been granted exemption from income tax for a period of 15 years. This marks a major beginning towards establishing India as the world’s rough diamond trading hub.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi recently inaugurated the Bharat Ratnam Mega Common Facility Centre at SEEPZ, Mumbai, as part of the transformational initiatives in the infrastructure sector. Spread across 1.25 lakh square feet, the centre is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities such as 3D printing, casting and refining. He said that the India Jewellery Park is a landmark project that is expected to attract an investment of around ₹50,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for one lakh people. The Maharashtra Government has also extended several incentives, including exemption from stamp duty, concessions on electricity and enhanced subsidy rates. He said that in 2025, the industry had reached ₹2.44 lakh crore, accounting for 6.3 per cent of the country’s merchandise exports. The industry is providing direct and indirect employment to around 75 lakh people.

Shri Amit Shah said that India has today emerged as a major source of jewellery imports for the United States, the Middle East, Hong Kong and Europe, and that this journey must be taken forward. He said that the Free Trade Agreements entered into by the Government of India’s Ministry of Commerce with the European Union, the United Arab Emirates, Australia, Oman and the United Kingdom can serve as a major avenue for expanding our trade. He said that with the support of the Government of India, we must move forward with confidence and determination to explore new markets, new avenues of trade and new opportunities. Today, India processes more than 90 per cent of the world’s cut and polished diamonds, which is the strongest testament to the courage and enterprise of India’s jewellery industry.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that times are changing and so are consumer trends, and this transformation presents a significant opportunity for the gems and jewellery trade. He said that jewellers should be prepared to seize the opportunities arising from these changes. He said that the era of lab-grown diamonds is now set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market. This represents a tremendous opportunity. He said that when the global jewellery trade underwent modernization, India was under colonial rule. Several countries moved ahead of us, including even smaller nations. But with the advent of the lab-grown diamond era, India has the necessary infrastructure, skills, capital and capable entrepreneurs. He said that we must prepare ourselves in such a way that the entire ecosystem and the complete manufacturing value chain for lab-grown diamonds are in the hands of Indians. Whether it is manufacturing the machines, producing lab-grown diamonds, making jewellery, or developing Indian brands and opening showrooms in cities across the world, the entire value chain should be within our reach. He said that Indian jewellery traders are fully capable of achieving this. Shri Shah said that the Government of India has already taken the initiative, while some enterprising traders in Surat and Mumbai have also taken the lead. The Governments of Gujarat and Maharashtra are bringing in supportive policies, and the Government of India will also introduce appropriate policies. He said that from manufacturing the machines to the showroom where the jewellery ultimately reaches a woman’s hand, India must have ownership of the entire ecosystem, and the industry must move forward with this vision and ambition. He said that merely increasing the pace of work will no longer be sufficient; the scale of operations must also be transformed. Shri Shah said that India should emerge as a pioneering industry in the new era of lab-grown diamonds, and Indian brands should become global brands, ensuring a strong presence for India and Indian jewellery traders in this global business. For this, the Modi Government is ready to provide all possible support.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that whenever Gujarat or India has faced a crisis, the jewellery industry has always stood wholeheartedly with society and the nation. The gems and jewellery industry has never shied away from contributing to the advancement and welfare of society. Whether it was a drought, a flood, a cyclone, water conservation, tree plantation, or ensuring that the children of artisans and employees receive education at the finest institutions, the industry has consistently contributed to the progress of society. For this, I wholeheartedly commend and congratulate the industry. He expressed hope that the leading industrial houses, young entrepreneurs and technologists present here would leave with the resolve that, in the diamond world of the future, the entire value chain should be built in India, and that the marketing chain across the world should also be led by Indian brands.

headline: Secretary, DAHD visits CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai; Calls for Strengthening Poultry Infrastructure, Training and Biosecurity
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Secretary, DAHD visits CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai; Calls for Strengthening Poultry Infrastructure, Training and Biosecurity

13 SEP 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, visited the Central Poultry Development Organisation (Western Region), Goregaon, Mumbai, today. Dr. Muthukumarasamy B., Joint Secretary, DAHD, and other senior officials of the Department were also present during the visit.

Shri Gangwar reviewed the functioning of CPDO (Western Region), including breeding, hatching, rearing and training activities, and inspected the hatchery, brooder houses, parent stock, feed plant and training facilities. The implementation of the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and other poultry development schemes was also reviewed. The Secretary emphasised the promotion of low-input technology birds, conservation of indigenous poultry germplasm, strengthening of biosecurity measures and modernisation of poultry infrastructure. Shri Gangwar directed that farmer-oriented training and the supply of quality chicks be further strengthened and appreciated the efforts of the CPDO team.

The Secretary interacted with poultry entrepreneurs trained at CPDO, Mumbai. The entrepreneurs shared their success stories and experiences, highlighting the contribution of CPDO’s training programmes towards entrepreneurship development in the poultry sector. Poultry management books in Hindi and Marathi were launched to promote access to technical knowledge and poultry-related learning in regional languages. Successful trainee students of CPDO, Mumbai, were felicitated for their achievements and inspiring success stories.

As part of the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, the dignitaries planted saplings, reaffirming their commitment towards environmental sustainability and a greener future. The dignitaries also visited the Poultry Gallery and held detailed discussions with officials of the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) regarding the redevelopment of CPDO, Mumbai. The programme concluded with an interaction with final-year BVSc & AH students of Mumbai Veterinary College on opportunities, challenges and emerging prospects in the veterinary and poultry sectors.

The Secretary also visited the Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (AQCS), Mumbai, which plays a critical role in maintaining the country’s biosecurity by preventing the ingress of animal diseases through the import of live animals and animal products. Shri Gangwar reviewed the functioning of the station and took stock of the ongoing and proposed development activities aimed at strengthening its infrastructure and operational capabilities. The visit provided valuable guidance for the future upgradation of CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai, as a Centre of Excellence in poultry development, training and technology dissemination.

headline: DAHD Reviews Lumpy Skin Disease Situation in NCT Delhi; Emphasises Coordinated Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

DAHD Reviews Lumpy Skin Disease Situation in NCT Delhi; Emphasises Coordinated Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures

13 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, today reviewed the Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) situation in the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi in coordination with the Delhi Animal Husbandry authorities. The review focused on the current disease situation, vaccination coverage, surveillance, treatment and strengthening of preventive and disease-control measures.

On 13th September, 2026 Animal Husbandry Commissioner (AHC), Dr. Naveena B. Maheswarappa, reviewed the disease situation with the Delhi Animal Husbandry authorities and emphasised the need for sustained vaccination, active surveillance and timely implementation of disease-control measures. He also stressed for close coordination with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), gaushalas and other stakeholders, particularly for effective management and vaccination of stray cattle and strengthening of biosecurity measures.

The LSD is sporadic in Delhi and presently under control, with low severity and good recovery among affected animals. No mortality has been reported among affected cattle. As on 13th September 2026, around 584 active cases are being reported, mainly among unvaccinated and vulnerable animals, including those with co-morbidities, weak nutritional status or those under stress.

More than 45,950 animals have been vaccinated against LSD in Delhi during 2026. Vaccination and other disease-control measures are continuing, with emphasis on timely vaccination, surveillance, isolation of affected animals, vector control, disinfection and biosecurity.

During the review, DAHD provided technical guidance to the Delhi authorities on vaccination, treatment and animal management and advised strengthening coordination with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), gaushalas and other stakeholders for effective management and vaccination of stray cattle, isolation of affected animals, vector control, disinfection/sanitization and implementation of biosecurity measures including establishment of physical check-post across neighbouring states for movement control.

Wider awareness activities involving animal owners, local representatives, NGOs, schools and other stakeholders were also emphasised to promote vaccination and good animal-husbandry practices.

The Department continues to maintain close coordination with States/UTs, regularly reviews the situation provide necessary assistance for effective prevention, control and containment of LSD. The disease situation across the country continues to be closely monitored.

headline: LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI SETS SAIL FROM LIVORNO, ITALY
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI SETS SAIL FROM LIVORNO, ITALY

13 SEP 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy’s sail training ship, INS Sudarshini, set sail from Livorno, Italy, on 12 Sep 2026 on completion of a successful port call. During her stay, the ship participated in a series of professional interactions and cross-training visits, strengthening bonds of friendship and maritime partnership between the two nations.

Admiral Giuseppe Berutti Bergotto, Chief of the Italian Navy, visited INS Sudarshini and interacted with the ship’s crew and trainees. He was briefed on the ship’s voyage and training activities. The Commanding Officer, INS Sudarshini, called on Rear Admiral Alberto Tarabotto, Commandant, Italian Naval Academy, and shared experiences from the ongoing expedition. Interactions were also held with Mr Luca Salvetti, Mayor of Livorno, and Mr Edoardo Lombardi, Vice Prefect of Livorno.

As part of the training exchanges, Indian sea trainees visited ITS Virginio Fasan and the Italian Naval Academy, while Italian naval personnel visited INS Sudarshini, fostering professional cooperation and mutual understanding. A deck reception was hosted onboard, attended by senior Italian naval officers, local authorities, diplomatic representatives and distinguished guests.

As INS Sudarshini continues her voyage as part of Lokayan 2026, she carries forward the spirit of maritime partnership and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

13 SEP 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the ‘Ganesh Gyanarthi Exhibition’ organised by the Asiatic Society of Mumbai in Mumbai today. On this occasion, Chief Minister of Maharashtra Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde, and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, along with several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the programme, Shri Amit Shah said that he has come to the Asiatic Society not as the Home Minister, but as a participant in the movement to carry forward the Indian knowledge tradition for thousands of years. Shri Shah expressed confidence that the Asiatic Society of Mumbai will become a bearer of the Indian knowledge tradition and spread it across the country.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that a nation which cannot protect its smriti, history, values, language, records and traditions, no matter how powerful it may be, does not take long to decline; and a nation which protects its smriti, history, traditions, values, records, language and grammar, no matter for how many years it remains enslaved, cannot truly be enslaved by anyone. He said that many forces attempted to erase India’s radiant knowledge, which stood ready to guide the world, but they could not succeed. Shri Shah said that the library of Nalanda can be burned; it can be reduced to ashes with such intensity that smoke rises for months, but the knowledge that has settled in people’s minds in the form of Shruti and Smriti cannot be destroyed by anyone.

Shri Amit Shah said that it is the culture of our country that when we are defeated, we move forward with patience; and when we are victorious, we try to integrate those whom we have conquered into our tradition without destroying their memories. He said that true knowledge is never held hostage by any ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology; if it is bound in any way, the very meaning of knowledge changes. Shri Shah said that knowledge should be free, uninhibited, and its proclamation should also be free and uninhibited. Therefore, instead of getting entangled in who founded the Asiatic Society and for what purpose, we should look at how the knowledge and collections that lie before us today can be used in the creation of a great India.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that to understand the Asiatic Society, one must also understand the term ‘Indology’. Numismatics, epigraphy, morphology, history, archaeology, linguistics, philosophy, literature, theology and grammar — all these together constitute Indology. Its purpose was not the same as that of the Indian knowledge tradition, whose goal is the welfare of the world and the universe. At that time, its objective was to understand the systems here so as to rule over the people of this land for a long period. Shri Shah said that when an external power studies a civilisation, it either studies it or defines it. There is a fundamental difference between the two. When one studies it, one also accepts it and changes oneself. But when one defines it, the question of what the objective of that definition is becomes extremely important. He said that after the term Indology came into existence, this danger remained constant in the initial years.

Shri Amit Shah said that India’s knowledge was not being written in India’s voice. It was being written in the language of the colonial perspective, whose purpose was to create a collective inferiority complex within society and to diminish the self-confidence of our people. He said that when the people’s self-confidence is low, resistance to long-term slavery does not arise. The Home Minister said that the interpretation of the capital of knowledge was also done from that viewpoint, but today the country has become independent. More than eighty years of independence have passed. The government has changed, the committee of the Asiatic Society has also changed, and now there is confidence that this storehouse of knowledge will be used for the welfare of the universe, the world and the country, and ensuring this is the responsibility of the institution’s new committee. Shri Shah said that by understanding the objectives of the Indian knowledge tradition, it must be seen how this knowledge can spread across the country and the entire world and gain acceptance. He said that based on the works of Bharat Ratna Pandit Pandurang Vaman Kane, ‘Kane Samagra’ should be compiled and every single word of it prepared for the coming generation, so that a new generation is built. He said that many such treasures exist in this institution.

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the British had intertwined knowledge and power with each other. Our task is to completely separate knowledge and power, so that power is created on the basis of knowledge, and the country is run on that very basis. Creating such a system is the work of the Asiatic Society. He said that it is often said in the country that history is being erased. Shri Shah said that he does not agree with those scholars. The process of decolonisation is not the erasure of history. It means placing history before the people once again in a complete, authentic manner and from an Indian perspective. This is decolonisation, and it must happen. Decolonisation does not mean erasure. Decolonisation means placing the truth before the world for the welfare of the world. Today we have moved towards decolonisation. He said that the Asiatic Society of Mumbai has illustrations of the Mahabharata, the Jain Kalpasutra, and such rare Buddhist texts that should have come out long ago.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Maharashtra is the land of the Saraswats. The primacy and importance of Saraswati are already inherent in the energy of this land. He said that the new team of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai is expected to expand the storehouse of knowledge that lies here. This expansion should take place from three perspectives. He said that the Asiatic Society should expand and the manuscripts available here should be fully linked with the Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript Mission launched by the Government of India. The Asiatic Society should explore the possibility of running a campaign to collect ancestral documents from villages across Maharashtra and from the homes of scholars, and linking them with the Gyan Bharatam Manuscript Survey. He said that research arrangements under the Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript Mission should be considered for all the departments associated with the manuscripts present here. Shri Shah said that research is essential on the vast knowledge contained in the manuscripts. These hold the power to take the country forward. He said that in the first informal meeting of the Gyan Bharatam Manuscript Mission, a Jain monk had said that the seed to make India the best in the world in economic and defence terms is contained in these very manuscripts. Arrangements for research on this must be made.

Shri Amit Shah said that he has told Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis to empower the Society. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India is providing every possible support and cooperation to the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and will continue to do so in the future. Shri Shah said that all such institutions existing in every village, every town and every state of the country should be linked with the Asiatic Society of Mumbai to create a shared repository of knowledge, so that it becomes available to students, researchers and scholars across the entire country.

headline: Prime Minister meets the Vice President of Uganda on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister meets the Vice President of Uganda on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi

13 SEP 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi held a warm and productive bilateral meeting today with H.E. Jessica Rose Epel Alupo, Vice President of the Republic of Uganda, on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

The two leaders reviewed bilateral ties between India and Uganda. They emphasized on the need to enhance cooperation in key priority areas through technology partnerships, capacity building, knowledge sharing, investment facilitation, and private-sector collaboration between the two countries. They also underlined that the development partnership between India and Uganda is a source of strength for both countries. Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s support to Uganda’s ‘Vision 2040’ for a transformed and prosperous Uganda. They also emphasized that close people-to-people ties continue to provide solidity to the partnership.

The two leaders called for closer bilateral engagement to champion the voice of the Global South. Prime Minister thanked Vice President for her participation in the Summit.

(Release ID: 2309761)
